title: AI's impact on fresh graduate hiring and support for graduates
asked: Assoc Prof Terence Ho asked whether AI adoption is prompting employers to slow hiring of fresh graduates from Institutes of Higher Learning in certain sectors or occupations, and whether the Ministry has plans to boost their employability and opportunities.
response: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong said employment rates of IHL fresh graduates have been broadly stable over the decade, with fluctuations from economic uncertainty, geopolitics and changing career aspirations. He said AI is reshaping the labour market but its specific impact on entry-level PMET jobs remains uncertain. IHLs are working with sector agencies and industry partners to keep curricula relevant, including AI competencies and core skills, and work-based learning such as the AI Apprenticeship Programme. Graduates can use Education and Career Guidance in IHLs and WSG/e2i services, and the GRIT Programme was introduced in 2025 for industry-relevant experience.
